Increasing Kernel reduces the edge of the swapped face. It essentially shrinks the mask to allow more of the Face A to show through. If you're seeing double eyebrows its because of a high kernel.

You want to reduce your kernel size to apply dilation to cover more of the FaceA's face with FaceB.

This assumes FaceA is the original and FaceB is the swap.

The setting description below is from FaceSwap:

-e EROSION_KERNEL_SIZE, --erosion-kernel-size EROSION_KERNEL_SIZE Erosion kernel size. (Masked converter only). Positive values apply erosion which reduces the edge of the swapped face. Negative values apply dilation which allows the swapped face to cover more space.
